conclusions: New location method uses original strict path normalization/file-to-parent handling, then one fresh fixed rev-parse through unchanged _execute.

Decoded output requires exactly two nonempty absolute locations. Invalid shape falls back to original root/common_directory(root); command/decode/resolve errors propagate without bypass. Root resolve remains strict and common resolve unchanged.

Engine batching only exact built-in LocalGitService without instance root/common_directory/_execute overrides. Subclasses and these existing instance overrides retain original dispatch and common-directory denial.

Constructor-local fresh tuple reused for sourceNone or exact same input; distinct input obtains its own fresh tuple. Different normalized roots must share common-directory identity. No cross-call tuple/status/graph cache or externally supplied trusted snapshot.
All subsequent storage/link/graph/cache guards, UOW/approval/checkpoint/transaction/durability paths unchanged.
semantic_limits: Valid two-line paths preserve whitespace rather than original .strip(); leading/trailing whitespace path acceptance can improve, not exact old normalization parity. UTF8 decode remains strict.
Malformed or separator-rich output shape uses legacy fallback; splitlines is not an unambiguous arbitrary pathname transport. No general newline-path support claimed.

Canonical common query now precedes distinct source-root validation; same-input explicit source observed once instead of twice. Exception ordering/call counts/transient filesystem observations can differ; no atomic snapshot or race-free guarantee.

Engine does not exclude instance overriding NEW root_and_common_directory; it is a trusted additive-method extension, not guaranteed built-in implementation. Including this name in the gate would be needed for that stronger claim. No preexisting override contract for new name found.
Dynamic class-level monkeypatches/stateful command counts outside instance/subclass parity guarantee.
Per-command timeout/Git env sanitization/hooks/fsmonitor/credential controls/error redaction unchanged; no new output-limit claim.

No tests, audits, probes, benchmarks or qualification workloads executed by reviewer. No speedup/5s browser cure, original14 or full86 closure, installed binding, two-round convergence or release readiness claim.
